title: No Verified Pet-Theft Record Supports a Responsible Raid Narrative
excerpt: No named arrest, seizure, verdict, or court record is supplied. Publishing invented raid details would betray stolen pets and families who need truth.
body_html:
Stolen companion animals deserve more than an invented raid story. No named arrest, seizure, verdict, court, police agency, date, quantity, or case number is supplied here. Claims about stun guns, poison baits, forged certificates, packed cages, or cross-provincial transport therefore cannot be published as verified facts.

Evidence must protect families

Pet theft is not abstract. When criminals steal dogs, families lose companions and face uncertainty about what happened next. That harm demands police records, court judgments, seizure reports, and transparent case status—not dramatic details without proof. Vietnamese families, rescuers, veterinarians, and local authorities can lead reform by reporting theft, preserving ownership evidence, and demanding public investigation.

Biosecurity needs precision

Rabies control and dog-trade oversight are related public safety concerns, but no record here establishes a direct link between a specific theft and a health event. Rabies spreads when infected saliva enters bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes. Wash any possible exposure with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes. Seek urgent medical care for post-exposure prophylaxis, including vaccine and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Once symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. World Health Organization rabies guidance.

Demand records. Demand quarantine enforcement. Demand protection for families and animals. SDE calls for complete abolition of the dog-meat trade by 2030. Sign the national petition and follow campaign updates as this public demand reaches decision-makers.
